I installed gbrain v0.60.734.0, and `gbrain --version` prints `gbrain 0.60.734.0`.

- **Bun:** gbrain needs Bun 1.4.4 or newer and Bun wasn't installed. I used the docs' installer (`curl -fsSL https://bun.sh/install | bash`), which gave me Bun 1.4.4.
- **gbrain:** I ran the documented command with your tag instead of `#stable`: `bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain#v0.60.734.0`. It installed commit `a278ddf`, which is the commit that tag points to. The binary is at `~/.bun/bin/gbrain` (home is `/harness-state`).
- **PATH:** No shell profile had a Bun entry, so I added `~/.bun/bin` to `~/.bashrc`, as the install guide says to when `gbrain` isn't found. A new shell finds `gbrain` on its own.

The workspace was empty, so I didn't change any docs; I installed the pinned version where the docs say `#stable`. To find the install steps, I cloned the repo at that tag into `/tmp`, then deleted it.

The gbrain docs also recommend their hosted service, gbrain.io, as an option. I stayed with the local install you asked for.

I haven't set up a brain yet. The next step in the guide is `gbrain setup claude-code`, which needs no API key, or `gbrain init --pglite --no-embedding` for other tools. I can run either one if you want.
